project_context: Create a standalone side-by-side HTML visual comparison page showing the CURRENT vs PROPOSED order card design. This is purely a static HTML preview page to allow the owner to review typography and layout changes. It does not modify any production React code.

typography.notes: Use Google Fonts CDN in the HTML head. Explicitly apply specific font sizes, weights, and colors as required by the spec to differentiate current and proposed designs.

layouts.page_structure: A single responsive page. Header section explaining the page context, a 2-column grid (Left: Current, Right: Proposed), and a bottom Changes Summary section.
layouts.column_layout: CSS Grid (grid-cols-2) with gap-8 for the side-by-side comparison.
layouts.card_layout: Flexbox column. Header row (flex row space-between), Item List (flex column), Status row (flex row timeline), Action buttons (CSS grid 2-columns or flex row wrap).

instructions_to_main_agent: 2. DO NOT modify any existing React components, TSX files, or package configurations.
3. Use Tailwind CSS via CDN (`<script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com"></script>`) in the head to build the UI quickly and accurately in one file.
4. Add a script tag to configure Tailwind theme to include the custom colors (`primaryOrange`, `primaryGreen`, `darkText`, etc.) and set Poppins as the sans font.
5. Use standard HTML elements (`div`, `span`, `button`) instead of framework components.
6. Data Requirement: Use exactly the requested dummy data: 'Butter Masala Dosa (1) + extra cheese slice', 'zone (1) kakzu (1) balluu (1) kaliya (1)', amounts like ₹242, ₹60.
7. Include AT LEAST 2 card types in each column: Dine-In card and Delivery/Aggregator card.

8. Annotations: Add small visually distinct badges (e.g., absolute positioned tooltips or small adjacent tags) in the PROPOSED column calling out the specific changes (e.g., '11px → 15px', 'Italic removed').
9. Summary Section: Include a 'CHANGES SUMMARY' table or list at the bottom detailing all 5 specified typographical changes clearly.

accessibility.contrast: Ensure the comparison text remains readable. Although Current specs use low-contrast grays, ensure the Proposed specs maintain high visibility (like #1A1A1A on white bg).
accessibility.data_testid: Add data-testid attributes to key sections, e.g., `data-testid="current-card"`, `data-testid="proposed-card"`, `data-testid="changes-summary"`.

UNIVERSAL_GUIDELINES_FOR_MAIN_AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. In frontend design, this creates what users call the 'AI slop' aesthetic. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight.
Dark colors look good when used independently without gradients. DO NOT use dark colors as gradients.
Don't make generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy.
Use glass-morphism effects with backdrop filters (12-24px blur) where appropriate, BUT DO NOT use complete transparent backgrounds for overlays or interactive items.
You MUST NOT apply universal transition. Eg: transition: all. This results in breaking transforms. Always add transitions for specific interactive elements like button, input excluding transforms.
You MUST NOT center align the app container, ie do not add .App { text-align: center; } in the css file. This disrupts the human natural reading flow of text.
Always use modern button styles like pill-shaped, or sharp button with interaction animations & color relevant to the app style.
NEVER: use AI assistant Emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭💡�🎯 etc for icons.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions, parallax effects, and entrance animations. Static = dead.
Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap.
Subtle grain textures, noise overlays, custom cursors, selection states, and loading animations: separates good from extraordinary.
All interactive and key informational elements MUST include a data-testid attribute to facilitate robust automated testing.
